title: Absolute file evidence is checked against each candidate directory directly, not relativized against root first
context: A prior version of this fix (dec_21fde3b22a, now corrected here) relativized an absolute related_files/scope_hint_file/affected_files entry against `root` alone (repoRelativeHint) before checking existence -- and claimed this 'prevents bypass'. Independent MR review (mr-complexity-reviewer, PR #76 second pass) verified by direct execution that the claim was false: the realistic case -- an agent in a linked worktree constructing an absolute path from ITS OWN cwd (the worktree), not from `root` -- relativizes to '../<worktree-dir>/...' against root, which repoRelativeHint's own outside-repo guard drops as "". The guard then saw an empty file list and stayed silent, reproducing the exact #54 bypass the fix claimed to close. Reproduced against all three tools (hunch_record_decision, hunch_record_correction, hunch_record_finding) before this fix.
decision: Generalize the existence check itself (existsUnder(dir, f) in src/mcp/server.ts) to understand BOTH relative and absolute entries directly, for whichever directory is under test (root, or each candidate sibling worktree in turn): a relative entry is joined onto that directory as before; an absolute entry is checked AS ITSELF, scoped via relative(dir, f) to confirm it actually falls under that specific directory's own tree, never joined. This makes an absolute path resolving under a sibling worktree's own tree DIRECT positive evidence for that worktree -- not a heuristic, not a guess -- while an absolute path outside every known worktree correctly contributes nothing (relativizes to "../..." everywhere, same as before). Superseded and REMOVED the correctionScopeHint/guardFiles dedup this replaces: with the guard no longer relativizing against root at all, there is only ONE remaining consumer of that normalization (buildCorrectionConstraint's own scope-glob construction, unrelated to the guard), so the exported dedup helper was reverted to a private, inlined implementation to avoid leaving unused public API surface.
consequences: An absolute path is now genuinely equivalent across all three write tools for the guard's purposes -- verified by direct MCP round-trips against fixture worktrees, not just unit-level function calls

misroutedWorktreeCandidates's public contract widened: callers now pass file evidence RAW (posix-normalized only), not pre-relativized -- a caller that still pre-relativizes before calling it will silently lose the sibling-worktree-absolute-path case again

The three call sites in src/mcp/server.ts (hunch_record_decision, hunch_record_correction, hunch_record_finding) all pass raw evidence now; none call repoRelativeHint/correctionScopeHint for the guard check anymore
alternatives_rejected: Keep the relativize-against-root approach and ALSO add a separate direct-match check as an additional signal layered on top (the shape an earlier review suggested) -- rejected as unnecessary complexity once it became clear the relativize-against-root heuristic was itself testing an unrealistic path shape (an absolute path constructed by joining root with a relative suffix, which no real caller does) rather than a case worth preserving alongside the real fix

Leave the false 'prevents bypass' claim in the graph and only fix the code -- rejected: this repo's whole thesis is that the graph must match what the code actually does; a corrected decision record was required, not just a corrected implementation
